# Handling of the GPT round 3 review report

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Original report | `review/metis-review-vong-3.md` (GPT, 03/10/2026): the conclusion is a conditional Go; 24 round two recommendations made up of 19 closed, 5 partly closed, 0 not closed, 0 with new defects arising; 31 new recommendations RF3-01 to RF3-31, of which 8 items are mandatory before the baseline is finalized; 10 questions I-01 to I-10 for the client |
| Applied to | Main BRD from 4.4 up to **4.5** (`brd/`), onboarding addendum from 1.0 up to **1.1** (`brd/`), 58 wireframes (`wireframes/`), style guide from 0.3 up to **0.4** (`brand/`), and the build kit (`brd/source/build.py`) |
| Product owner's constraint | Keep assumption A-07 unchanged: an agency of about 40 developers, no scope cut because of team size. The round three report complies with this constraint and proposes no scope cut |
| How it was handled | Verified each claim against the real files before editing, then applied **all 31 items**, not only the 8 mandatory items. Every claim that could be checked was correct; no item had to be disputed. Two items were already partly in the documents from before and only needed the missing part added |
| Biggest finding of this round | The gap is no longer missing screens but **a specification contract that can be read in two ways**: a sentence asserting the equivalence of canvas and list that cannot be broken down into tests; a role that resolves to "the only person holding it" while also lumping in the case where nobody holds it; a publish check that lets through a framework whose own schedule contradicts itself; and a screen coverage figure that is read as evidence of behavior |

Result notation: **Applied** (edited exactly as recommended), **Applied with adjustment** (edited another way but closing the same gap, with the reason recorded), **Already partly present** (the document already said it, only the missing part added).

## Eight mandatory items before the baseline is finalized

| Code | Verification before editing | Result | Where edited |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RF3-01** The thirty-minute measurement contract | Correct. The goal section writes "any client sets up its company in Metis in 30 minutes" while the target table says "30 minutes or less (median)"; the measurement requirement says "time while the session is paused or closed is not counted", so the metric can look better by closing the tab | Applied | Addendum §4.1 fully rewritten: activation is **a four-part event** that must hold within the same session; **eligible session** has clear entry conditions, excluding trial tenants by a flag, not by name; **five clocks** measured separately (active open, elapsed, user input, processing wait, external dependency), the clock does not stop when the tab is closed; thirty minutes is active open time and the target is **the share of passing sessions plus the distribution**, never the median alone. ONB-26 rewritten as an event schema. §19.2 changed to activation rate, share within target, median together with percentiles 75 and 90. The title, §1, §1.2 and §2 change accordingly. Screens 46, 47, 52 drop the stopwatch; screen 57 separates eligible, activated, active open and elapsed |
| **RF3-02** The contract for granting permissions at launch | Correct. ONB-15 says "grant the approved roles" but nowhere defines how a role becomes approved; BR-44 only requires that there be an approver; privileged roles are not classified | Applied | ONB-15 rewritten: every role first exists as a **proposed role grant** with a source, a recipient and an **access diff** between the current permissions and the proposed permissions; ordinary roles are approved in batches, **privileged roles are approved by person name**; the server rechecks each grant against the permission matrix at commit time. Added BR-51, D-41 (list of privileged roles), the entity `Proposed role grant` in the data model, one acceptance item and one new risk. Screen 52 has an Access changes section with three privileged grants that clearly state now and after |
| **RF3-03** Status of the process framework in the starting pack | Correct. ONB-27 says the pack contains process frameworks and a Draft workspace built from the pack is ready to activate; BLD-16 says only the Workspace Owner may publish. It does not say which version the pack carries | Applied | ONB-27 rewritten: the pack **references the immutable built-in Published version held by the provider**, applying the pack creates no publication event in the workspace; when the customer or the AI edits it, the edited version becomes a workspace draft and the Workspace Owner publishes it under BLD-16. Main BRD BLD-09 states clearly that a template or pack references the provider's version; one line added to the amendments table in §13 and to §7.4 |
| **RF3-04** The meaning of the word delete | Correct. The fourth acceptance criterion of ONB-22 says that after the files are deleted, "each source link keeps only the file name and the quoted passage". The quoted passage is source content | Applied | ONB-22 and D-38 split into **two separately named actions**: delete the original files (deletes the binary, keeps the metadata and the quoted passage) and delete the source content (deletes the binary, the extracted text, the fragments and the quoted passage; keeps the source id, the hash and the "source removed" label); both state clearly what the audit retention D-34 and the backup purge still keep, instead of promising that everything is deleted. §11.5 and screen 56 follow the same wording |
| **RF3-05** The barrier against instruction injection | Correct. ONB-24 relies on "instruction-like text is removed and reported" as the only barrier at the model layer | Applied | ONB-24 rewritten into **three layers separated by code outside the model**: extraction (the model sees the text but has no tool to write, fetch or read other records), validation (checks the schema, the cited source and the permission matrix), writing (a deterministic orchestrator calls the setup tool). Instruction-like text is **quarantined with its source, not deleted**, because deleting imperative sentences deletes the very governance rules that need to be read. §9.1 has a new pipeline table and a paragraph stating clearly why the detector cannot be the boundary. ONB-25 adds a corpus owner, a format and language matrix, pinning of the provider, model, prompt and parser dependency versions, and a poisoned fixture pack |
| **RF3-19** Equivalence of canvas and list | Correct. The second criterion of BLD-13 has only one sentence "Every editor action can be done in the list view without a pointer" | Applied | BLD-13 broken down into a **parity matrix**: one row per operation, made up of the mouse gesture, the keyboard command, the action in the list and the command sent to the server, for node, lane, connection and route point. The matrix becomes the tenth item of the foundation contract pack §18.4 with its path and fixture; BR-41 refers to the matrix; §21 acceptance goes row by row. Screen 58 has a ten-row table |
| **RF3-20** Resolving a role or title to a person | Correct. The second criterion of BLD-14 says "resolves to the one project member holding it; otherwise it stays empty", which lumps together nobody matching and several people matching | Applied | BLD-14 changed to a **typed assignment selector** (workspace role or normalized member title) with **three outcomes**: resolved, missing, ambiguous; ambiguous blocks the build until the PM chooses, Metis never takes the first person; renaming a title keeps an alias or explicitly disables it. Added D-40 (matching rule), two entities in §15.1, two values in §15.2, and a note in §14 saying that a selector is not a permission. Screen 58 has three states in the build preview |
| **RF3-30** Contrast of hint text | Correct. `tokens.css` line 18 says faint 2.6 "never meaningful text", but `style-guide.md` line 193 assigns that same color to the hint text of input fields, and hint text is meaningful text | Applied | Hint text moves to `muted` (5.2), `faint` is left only for disabled components and decorative details, with the WCAG 1.4.3 reason right in the color table. Edited `tokens.css`, `style-guide.md` sections 3.2 and 6, `style-guide.html` (added `::placeholder`), `wireframes/assets/wireframe.css` in three places; new rule: a hint that has to be read for a long time becomes permanent helper text. Also deleted one dead CSS rule that still used faint |

## Ten questions for the client in part I

All ten questions were answered with the recommendation recorded in the documents, in the way done in round two; the product owner can change them again.

| Question | How it was handled |
|---|---|
| I-01 What "Any client" means: every tenant or only tenants that meet the entry conditions, and what the conditions are | §4.1 defines an eligible session by four entry conditions and states clearly that a session outside the conditions is still measured but reported separately |
| I-02 Which roles are privileged and must be reviewed by person name | D-41 lists: Tenant Admin, Workspace Owner, Executive or ExCo, Portfolio Manager or PMO, and every role that can approve, publish or change permissions |
| I-03 What evidence is enough to call a budget or date approved | BR-53 and ONB-10: the document type the customer confirms as authoritative, the approval stamp, the date, and the approver if the document records one |
| I-04 Whether the process framework in the pack is a built-in Published version or a clone, and who publishes | ONB-27: references the provider's built-in Published version; if edited it becomes a workspace draft and the Workspace Owner publishes under BLD-16 |
| I-05 Which field groups must never be Assumed or Default | D-42 and BR-52: identity and access, baseline budget and dates together with source authority, approver, quorum and routing, and settings that cannot be changed later |
| I-06 Which types of data the customer wants to allow or block from going to the LLM | D-43: default masking for four groups, plus a list of data classes that are blocked outright, and a statement that detection is not perfect |
| I-07 Whether "Setup complete" means closing every task or only the mandatory tasks | ONB-17: two separate numbers, launch complete at the time of commit and follow-through complete when every mandatory item is closed; a deferred item stays outside the denominator until its trigger occurs |
| I-08 Whether the BYO-AI path accepts a quoted passage reported back by the customer's AI as evidence | New Q-19, with an interim recommendation in §12.4: a high-impact value must be confirmed by a person, and the label says Customer AI so as not to imply that Metis has read the document |
| I-09 Whether any attention debt threshold blocks launch | ONB-15 criterion five: an unconfirmed high-impact value blocks launch; ordinary values do not block but are shown by risk group together with the owner, and an overloaded owner is named |
| I-10 Whether title matching is exact normalized or a mapping kept by the customer | D-40: match the role first, then the normalized title (trimmed, case-folded, accent-folded), plus an alias list kept by the customer; when several people share a title the PM chooses at each build and the choice is recorded |
